title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 40-43). C is the k-linear category with objects C^i and generators d^i: C^i -> C^{i+1}, subject to d^{i+1} d^i = 0. In modern terms it is the path category of the linear quiver A_∞ with zero relations. K denotes its additive/Karoubian envelope. The guiding fact (Prop. 1) is that a k-linear functor C -> B is the same thing as a cochain complex in B.

Previous page: the contravariant Yoneda functor α^·: C^op -> Ab_k^· sends C^i to the contractible complex K^i = (k --id--> k) in degrees i, i+1. Its essential image (after Karoubi completion) is the acyclic complexes of free modules of finite type. Ex. 2 uses the covariant representables Hom(L,-) instead, giving a fully faithful functor β into chain complexes.

Top of this page: β is computed on generators.
- β(C^i) is again a two-term complex k -> k in two consecutive degrees, with β(d^i) given by id_k in the appropriate degree.
- C^0 is a boundary case, for the nonnegatively indexed version: β(C^0) has an isolated k in degree 0.
- A crossed-out paragraph would have used the category of complexes itself as a possible way of constructing an example of a pair (C^·, Č^·).

'Passage de l'exemple 1 à l'exemple 2': the k-linear dual M ↦ M^∨ = Hom_k(M,k) is an anti-equivalence of finite free k-modules with themselves. Applied degreewise, it identifies cochain complexes of f.t. free modules with chain complexes of such (with the parenthetical care about Z_0 versus Z^i being free). The diagram says this duality turns α_· : C -> K_· into (α^·)^op : C -> (K^·)^op, i.e. the triangle commutes up to isomorphism. Grothendieck dismisses the verification as trivial.

Prop. 2: there is a perfect pairing, functorial in x ∈ K, given by composition:
  Hom(C^n, x) × Hom(x, C^{n+1}) -> Hom(C^n, C^{n+1}) ≅ k (spanned by d^n).
Equivalently α_n(x) ≅ α^{n+1}(x)^∨, where (left margin) α_·(x) = Hom(C_·, x) and α^·(x) = Hom(x, C^·), compatibly with differentials.

Check on generators x = C^m.
- Hom(C^n, C^m) ≠ 0 only for m = n, n+1.
- Hom(C^m, C^{n+1}) ≠ 0 only for m = n, n+1.
- For m = n the pairing is id × d ↦ d; for m = n+1 it is d × id ↦ d. Both are nondegenerate.
- By additivity and passing to retracts, the pairing is perfect on all of K.

Modern reading: Hom(C^n, -)^∨ ≅ Hom(-, C^{n+1}), i.e. a Serre functor S with S(C^n) = C^{n+1}. Equivalently, the Nakayama functor sends the projective P_n to the injective I_{n+1}. This reflects the Frobenius nature of the category of complexes, whose projective-injectives are the contractible two-term complexes.

Next page (Prop. 3): F(x) ≅ Hom^·_k(α^·(x), C_F^·), with Hom^· defined as an end/equalizer. This is the weighted-limit reconstruction of a k-linear functor from the complex it classifies; the purpose is to compute F_C(x) for a complex C^· in B.
errors: As transcribed, Prop. 2 reads Hom(C^n,x) × Hom(x,C^n) -> Hom(C^n,C^n) ≅ k. That pairing is not perfect: for x = C^{n+1} one side is k and the other 0. The correct and consistent form, which the image also appears to support, pairs Hom(C^n,x) with Hom(x,C^{n+1}) into Hom(C^n,C^{n+1}) ≅ k.
Degree bookkeeping for β(C^i) and especially the boundary object C^0 is garbled on the page. The page itself does not make clear whether the generic formula needs i ≥ 1 and which degrees carry k.

ideas.what: Cochain complexes in B = k-linear functors from the 'walking complex' category C (quiver A_∞ with relations d²=0); Yoneda embedding into complexes, with image the contractible/acyclic f.t. free complexes
ideas.modern_name: Representations of a quiver with relations; universal (walking) complex; Yoneda/Morita for linear categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; Gabriel (quiver representations), Mitchell 'Rings with several objects' 1972, Kelly (enriched categories)

ideas.what: Degreewise k-duality identifying f.t. free cochain complexes with chain complexes, compatible with the two Yoneda embeddings
Perfect composition pairing Hom(C^n,x) × Hom(x,C^{n+1}) -> k, i.e. Hom(C^n,-)^∨ ≅ Hom(-,C^{n+1})
ideas.modern_name: Serre functor / Nakayama functor (shift by one) for the category of contractible complexes; Frobenius property of the category of complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bondal–Kapranov (Serre functors, 1989); Happel (Frobenius categories, Nakayama functor, 1987-88)

ideas.modern_name: Weighted limit / end formula, Kan extension

missed.claim: Grothendieck records, for the walking-complex category, a functorial perfect duality Hom(C^n,x)^∨ ≅ Hom(x,C^{n+1}). This is a Serre-functor-type statement made more than a decade before Bondal–Kapranov formalised Serre functors. It is an elementary instance, not a general theory.
missed.quote: Prop 2 On a une dualité parfaite fonctorielle en M ∈ Ob K ... Hom(C^n,x) × Hom(x,C^{n+1}) → Hom(C^n,C^{n+1}) ≃ k
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest only: it shows Grothendieck thinking of complexes as modules over a small linear category with Serre-type duality. The mathematics itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is elementary bookkeeping for the linear category classifying complexes: Yoneda, duality and a composition pairing. The Serre-functor flavour of Prop. 2 is a mildly interesting anticipation, but it is a trivial special case well known in representation theory.
transcription_corrections: Prop. 2 second factor and target should read Hom(x, C^{n+1}) and Hom(C^n, C^{n+1}) ≅ k, not Hom(x, C^n) and Hom(C^n, C^n).
Top line likely reads 'On trouve ici que ... i ≥ 1' (generic case) rather than 'i≤4 i≠1'.
'(d^i_i) = id_k, i ≥ 10' is probably '(d^i)_{i} = id_k, i ≥ 0' or similar degree condition.
'Mod_k ≃ Ab_k' in the duality line is better read as M ↦ M^∨, an anti-equivalence of finite free k-modules with themselves.
The diagram reads α_· : C -> K_· (≈), (α^·)^op : C -> K^{·op}, with an equivalence K_· ≃ K^{·op}.
